label: Gerard: starting repaglinide or a sulfonylurea after age 75
title: Starting repaglinide or a sulfonylurea after age 75
statement: It is necessary not to initiate treatment with a hypoglycaemic drug (repaglinide or sulfonylurea) in a patient over 75 years old.

plain_summary: Review a new prescription for repaglinide or a sulfonylurea for someone with type 2 diabetes who was older than 75 at the start.

needs_facts.meets: Documented type 2 diabetes at the time of treatment.

needs_facts.what: Repaglinide or sulfonylurea supply under review: start or repeat and age at start
needs_facts.meets: A dated note, a new-start direction or the pharmacist confirms that the supply under review started this medicine when the patient was older than 75.

options.words: This supply started the medicine when the patient was older than 75
This supply started the medicine at age 75 or younger
This was a repeat of established treatment

rule_for_models: Flag a supply of repaglinide or a sulfonylurea that started treatment after age 75 in a patient with type 2 diabetes. Cite the supply, the diagnosis and the start evidence from the directions, a dated note or the pharmacist’s answer about that supply. A repeat, a start at age 75 or younger, or confirmed absence of type 2 diabetes gives no finding for that supply. If the other evidence fits but the diagnosis, start or age at the start is missing or unknown, report a possible finding and ask for that detail.
cannot_be_seen: A first visible dispensing may be a refill from a prescription started elsewhere. The record may omit the original start date and the person's treatment goals.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm when repaglinide or the sulfonylurea was started and review its suitability given the person’s age at the time and risk of hypoglycaemia?
